band_change_evidence_test.required: at least 2 independent sources with at least 1 at sourceTier >= 4
band_change_evidence_test.reason: FAIL. Two independent sources were located — Harvey's own BigLaw Bench hallucination post at tier 3 and independent reviewer comparisons at tier 2, plus Law.com trade coverage at tier 3. No source at tier 4 or above was obtained. Harvey AI cannot be verified at tier 4 in either direction.

key_evidence: Harvey AI does one thing that most labs in this study do not: it publishes its own error rate. Its BigLaw Bench post states that its Assistant model hallucinates about 1 claim in 500. Publishing that is not reputationally convenient.
Independent reviewers push back on the framing. They note Harvey has not published independent hallucination benchmarks, and that on third-party comparisons it is 'consistently good, never great'.

The access picture is thin. The Pro Bono Institute reports Harvey has a legal aid programme but that access is limited, and that free tools remain more accessible to legal aid organisations. Meanwhile roughly 70% of the AmLaw 10 uses Harvey.
That gap is why Equity scores 2.0 out of 5 — the lowest dimension. A stated intention to support nonprofits does not yet match where the product actually goes.
No source above tier 3 was obtained for Harvey. The score falls 19.6 points, and most of that is missing disclosure rather than located harm.

evidence.claim: On BigLaw Bench tasks, Harvey's Assistant model hallucinates around 1 in 500 claims, or 0.2%, while foundation models hallucinate between 1 in 150 and 1 in 110.
Harvey publishes a BigLaw Bench claim of 91% accuracy, but on published benchmark scores it is consistently good, never great, and Harvey hasn't published independent hallucination benchmarks.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A DOWNGRADE. No score change is proposed for application. The published 48.4 is a never-assessed uniform-seed placeholder shared byte-for-byte with seven other ai-labs entities at consecutive alphabetical ranks; the rank is an artefact of the tie. No adverse conduct was located. The entire gap measures disclosure, not conduct. Applying a one-off baseline reset on evidence-absence alone would convert a calibration problem into a conduct finding, which the anti-false-positive screen forbids. Referred for coordinator-level calibration of the ai-labs 60.9 and 48.4 uniform-seed clusters. rotation-state composite/band/rank left at the PUBLISHED values.
